questionText: Which of the following standard C library functions will always invoke a system call when executed from a single-threaded process in a UNIX/Linux operating system?
explanation:
Explanation:

(A) exit: The exit() function performs user-space cleanup (such as flushing stdio streams) and then strictly invokes the _exit or exit_group system call to terminate the process. Therefore, it always invokes a system call.

(B) malloc: malloc() manages dynamic memory in user space using a memory pool. It only issues a system call (such as brk or mmap) when the pre-allocated pool cannot satisfy the memory request. Thus, it does not always invoke a system call.

(C) sleep: The sleep() library function suspends execution of the calling process by invoking underlying kernel kernel time/delay system calls such as nanosleep(). Thus, it always invokes a system call.

(D) strlen: strlen() iterates over a null-terminated string to count its characters entirely within user-space memory, so it never invokes a system call.

Hence, the correct options are A and C.
